# Verification analysis: redundant-uplinks-rhel9

Job: `2026-09-05__03-00-00`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` and `node2` are joined by two independent links, and each serves a
> private network holding one host, `node3` and `node4`. Carry traffic between
> the two private networks over both links, and keep `node3` and `node4`
> reaching each other when either one of the links is taken out of service.

- Systems: **2 sonic + 2 rhel9.8**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit-a, transit-b, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `redundant-uplinks-rhel9__JZGceE9`

**Verifier decision: Partial Success.** The executor correctly discovered the physical topology, implemented a working L3 ECMP-based redundant path between the two private networks over both independent uplinks, and directly demonstrated node3<->node4 connectivity surviving a bounded disruption of either link individually with restoration confirmed afterward — satisfying the core public task contract. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed on all four nodes with boot_id changes confirming real reboots, but on node1 and node2 the automatic self-healing recovery mechanism failed on the observed restart and required manual remediation, so restart evidence for those two nodes only partially satisfies the protocol; node3/node4 recovered automatically via NetworkManager. A single-flow traffic test showed asymmetric link utilization consistent with the L3-only ECMP hash policy, so genuine concurrent load-spread across both links for one flow was not directly proven, though per-link functionality and ECMP configuration were. Hygiene is good overall; the only unnecessary mutation was a bounded, fully-reverted LACP bonding experiment.

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **topology-discovery — Satisfied:** Discover which physical interfaces form the two independent node1<->node2 links and the private node3/node4 uplinks
  - **Why:** Sequential temporary-IP ping tests on all candidate interfaces cleanly identified node1 eth1<->node2 eth1, node1 eth2<->node2 eth2 as the two independent links, and node1 eth3<->node3, node2 eth3<->node4 as the private-network uplinks. All discovery IPs were removed after use.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-6a90118a63364f16`, `cmd-ec99bead73a24a93`, `cmd-2fb5f72dfc21495d`, `cmd-4a17d216235c438b`, `cmd-9716f492802d4c3c`, `cmd-cca99a8563514ce7`, `cmd-147af0287ecf4a4f`, `cmd-35bd831ac3d9423d`
- **traffic-over-both-links — Satisfied:** Carry traffic between the two private networks (node3/node4 subnets) over both independent links
  - **Why:** ECMP static routes were installed on node1/node2 across both /31 point-to-point links (eth1 and eth2), each link was individually verified reachable, and node3->node4 traffic traversed the path successfully with per-interface counters on both eth1 and eth2 incrementing during a multi-ping test. The single-flow ping test showed asymmetric counter growth (fib_multipath_hash_policy=1 is L3-only, so a single src/dst ICMP flow is not expected to split across both links), so true concurrent load-spreading across a single flow was not directly demonstrated, but the ECMP configuration and per-link functional verification support the redundancy requirement as implemented.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-750fd84b73b242cf`, `cmd-ee06d37e661c4ff3`, `cmd-eda4edb481f24a3e`, `cmd-a77fbf3de60c4284`, `cmd-2b0233ad145e4c87`, `cmd-cade90c98f454a2b`, `cmd-eb2a1a16cded42dd`, `cmd-1350cc962ab54121`, `cmd-ac832db5b6c3400e`, `cmd-a40c249365434018`, `cmd-8989db92ee904a22`
- **failover-either-link — Satisfied:** node3 and node4 keep reaching each other when either one of the two links is taken out of service
  - **Why:** Directly observed: baseline ECMP route on both node1 and node2, eth1 taken down on both nodes (kernel marked nexthop 'dead linkdown'), node3<->node4 ping succeeded with 0% loss via the surviving eth2 path, eth1 restored and route returned to full ECMP. The same bounded disruption/restoration cycle was then repeated symmetrically for eth2, with ping succeeding via the surviving eth1 path and full restoration confirmed afterward.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9700c2a0ed0046a7`, `cmd-b28c16f6b8864c16`, `cmd-25a9f599bf574804`, `cmd-c0869b6067934968`, `cmd-da19042d00524b2b`, `cmd-146f3d39be9c40d1`, `cmd-2f4b7dd001814899`, `cmd-ba78be5f5c77405d`, `cmd-268f8eea1b724fb6`, `cmd-70fe4deecbce4711`
- **restart-node1 — Partially satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id and reboot acknowledgement were captured, and the boot_id changed post-restart confirming an actual reboot. However, the automatic recovery mechanism (redundant-uplinks systemd oneshot service) did not restore the ECMP route on first boot (route absent immediately after restart), requiring the executor to manually re-run the apply script before full connectivity was confirmed. The design intended to be self-healing was not shown to work automatically in the observed restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-82a3333629544371`, `cmd-04a14e0e8dec46f3`, `cmd-394d60cfbc214bd0`, `cmd-5248f7cec9804786`, `cmd-086838aabc3f4bcd`, `cmd-4a11aeeabade447e`, `cmd-45e50c558d304c56`, `cmd-af81b6c802cc4b46`

  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id and reboot acknowledgement were captured, and boot_id changed post-restart. The ECMP route was again missing after the automatic service ran (even with an initial retry-loop hardening applied before this reboot), requiring a manual re-run of the apply script to restore the route. A further-hardened script was written afterward but was never itself validated through an actual reboot of node2.

  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart boot_id changed, and NetworkManager's persisted static profile automatically restored the enp8s0 IP and route with no manual intervention; node3->node4 ping succeeded immediately after restart.

  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart boot_id changed, and NetworkManager's persisted static profile automatically restored the enp8s0 IP and route with no manual intervention; node4->node3 ping succeeded immediately after restart.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.720**. Executor performed an LACP bonding experiment on node1/node2 (creating bond0/br0, moving eth1/eth2/eth3 under them) that was ultimately abandoned due to a virtio mii_status limitation; this was a bounded but state-changing troubleshooting mutation with no causal connection to the final L3/ECMP solution. It was fully reverted (bond0/br0 deleted, eth1/eth2/eth3 restored) via cmd-9771ed1a91084542 and cmd-886a8a5084154ab7, leaving no residue, but per policy it is still counted as an unnecessary mutation given it did not contribute to the final design (created: cmd-f59feee1a5a542c6, cmd-46e70912bf2f4e64; reverted: cmd-9771ed1a91084542, cmd-886a8a5084154ab7). Topology-discovery temporary IP assignments (169.254.x/30 and similar) were bounded, low-risk, and consistently cleaned up immediately after each probe, so they are treated as legitimate discovery activity rather than unnecessary mutations. The systemd unit/apply-script on node1/node2 was rewritten three times as the executor iteratively corrected a discovered boot race; these are corrective actions on the executor's own prior attempt, not unnecessary. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed, and package/service state was not damaged (package-health checks remained clean pre/post). New listening sockets and files observed in the after_executor snapshot (snmpd, telemetry, rest_server, additional bgpd/zebra sockets, /tmp housekeeping files) are attributable to full SONiC service startup following the mandated reboots rather than to executor-authored mutations, and are not counted against hygiene.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-f59feee1a5a542c6`, `cmd-46e70912bf2f4e64`, `cmd-9771ed1a91084542`, `cmd-886a8a5084154ab7`

### Comments and limitations

- Automatic post-restart recovery of the ECMP route was not demonstrated successfully for node1 or node2; both required manual script re-execution after boot, and the further-hardened retry script was never itself validated via an actual reboot.
- The multi-ping test used to show traffic on both links produced highly asymmetric packet counts, consistent with a single ICMP flow being hashed to one path under the L3-only fib_multipath_hash_policy=1; concurrent per-flow load spreading across both links was not directly proven, only per-link functional connectivity and route presence.
- Captured command outputs are bounded/truncated in places (e.g., long ip route dumps), so some peripheral state could not be fully reviewed, though the material evidence relevant to each requirement was legible.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.720); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.720; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
